10.0.0.en: "And He arose from thence, and cometh": that is, He left Capernaum and headed south to Judea after crossing the river Jordan. And as was the Lord Christ's custom, He began to teach and preach to all who gathered around Him.

10.1.0.en: "And the Pharisees came ... tempting Him": this also shows us that the Pharisees were following Him, not in order to benefit, but in order to test Him and catch Him in mistakes. Therefore they chose a subject that represents a social controversy, despite the clarity of the commandment about it, namely the subject of divorce.

10.2.0.en: In the wisdom of Christ and its perfection, He answered their question with a question, namely: what is the commandment that God gave to Moses? They answered with the confidence of teachers that the Law permitted divorce, on condition that a document be written for it, so that by it the woman might marry again if she wished (and it was the custom that the man would first go to one of the wise men to absorb his anger before the bill of divorce was written).

10.3.0.en: The Lord Christ makes clear what God's purpose was in marriage, and why there was the exception and the permission of divorce. For God, in His plan and purpose, created one man and one woman, that each might belong to the other. But because of the people's turning away from God, the decline of their spiritual level, and their comparison with the pagan peoples who permit adultery and polygamy, God permitted them divorce, but not out of the pleasure of His heart, but perhaps to protect the wife from being killed, or the man from turning to idolatry.

10.4.0.en: To confirm His answer, the Lord Christ used the same words that Adam uttered in (Gen 2:24) after the creation of Eve - words which the Pharisees know well - and the meaning of these words is as follows:

10.4.1.en: "For this cause": that is, for the completion of the sacrament of marriage.

10.4.2.en: "Shall a man leave": that is, the man must become independent of his father's house in order to build his new family. And this independence or leaving does not mean neglecting our duties toward our parents in caring for them, for marital love does not conflict with the commandment to honor parents.

10.4.3.en: "One flesh": it points to the splendor of the Christian marital union, for by the descent of the Holy Spirit in the prayer of the crowning, the two become one on the level of soul, body and spirit.

10.5.0.en: After the Lord Christ had made clear the picture of the wonderful marital union in (v. 8), He also makes clear that God is the founder of this union and the One who joins it together, and He is the One who works with the married couple, and in them, so that they may become one flesh. Consequently, man cannot annul a bond or covenant that God established and witnessed. But the Christian must strive together with the work of God's grace in the sacrament of marriage, and struggle in controlling himself, offering love, and bearing the shortcomings and weaknesses of the other however hard this may be. For Christian marriage is not for the pleasing of the self and its desires, but is a call to the breaking of self and selfishness and to submission to the other, as the Church charges us in the prayer of the crowning: "Let each of you submit to the other." Only then does man's will meet God's good will.

10.6.0.en: As happened often, and in private, the disciples asked the Lord Christ for a further explanation of this dialogue, and He added that the real motive for seeking divorce is that the feelings or desires of the man and the woman are moved toward another party, so he seeks to fulfill his desire by divorcing the first in order to be joined to the second. Therefore God considered divorcing in order to marry to be nothing but the sin of adultery before Him, even if society approves of this second marriage.

10.6.1.en: My beloved brother ... have you understood now why our Church does not permit divorce except for the cause of adultery? For the Church is entrusted with Christ's commandment, and the pressure of society on her does not move her. And instead of resorting to the easy solutions of divorce, we must establish sound spiritual concepts, and prepare generations and youth to understand the meaning of Christian marriage.

10.7.0.en: "And they brought": what is meant, of course, is the fathers and mothers of the children, for they felt the holiness of Christ and His blessing. Therefore each of them hurried to bring his children to obtain the blessing by Christ's touching them. And we may infer that this situation caused a crowding and commotion that made the disciples rebuke these parents.

10.8.0.en: "Much displeased": let it never be understood from this expression as the nervous human emotion into which we may fall in our weakness. But when Christ saw how the disciples had shocked the children's parents with coldness, He said to them: "Suffer the little children to come unto Me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God." That is, these children, by their simplicity and purity - which we adults may have lost - have come to own the Kingdom before us.

10.9.0.en: "Verily I say unto you": it is the expression Christ always used before declaring an important spiritual truth, and here it is: that childhood is a meaning and not an age, so none will enter the Kingdom of God except he who enjoys the virtues of little children, such as innocence, simplicity and trust, which are marks that distinguish the pure children of God, and which the evil world does not know. For God wants from us simplicity, spontaneity and the trust of faith in prayer and in speaking with Him; likewise He wants our dealings with others to be free of craftiness and of the world's satanic wisdom, but to be frank and simple, and not lacking the wisdom of the Holy Spirit ... And after this teaching, the Lord embraced the children with His great tenderness, and granted them His divine blessing.

10.9.1.en: My beloved God ... I long for my childhood in You ... would that I were one of those children, touching Your knees with my hand, and You touching the locks of my hair with Your hand, so that the current of Your holiness would run through my whole being...

10.9.2.en: My God ... I know that You have given me much, but I cannot hold back the longing of my heart to throw myself into Your tender embrace!

10.10.0.en: As the Lord Christ was going out on His way to Jerusalem, a man came and worshiped Him, asking Him about the way to eternal life. And the word "ran" shows that his coming to Christ was out of eagerness and a real motive for knowledge ... and the word "knelt" points to his respect and veneration for Christ.

10.11.0.en: Sadly, the enemies of Christianity, throughout the ages, have exploited this verse to deny divinity to Christ. To these we say that Christ declared His divinity clearly, as it is in (Jn 10:30): "I and My Father are one."

10.11.1.en: And to explain what Christ said, we must briefly become acquainted with a Jewish background of this time ... for the priests and the Pharisees forbade the people to use the name of God in conversation, and to be content with mentioning His titles, so they would say the Blessed ... the Most High ... the Good ... and so on.

10.11.2.en: Therefore, when this man addressed Christ in the previous verse, saying: "Good Master", Christ stopped him in this verse, saying: "Why callest thou Me good?" Is it because you:

10.11.3.en: realize that I am God, and so ascribe to Me the absolute goodness which belongs to God alone?

10.11.4.en: speak to Me as people are accustomed, in courtesy toward those they respect, by applying attributes and titles to them?

10.12.0.en: Christ was not waiting for an answer from the man, but answered his question that the way to the Kingdom is keeping God's commandments and doing them, and the Lord Christ mentioned some of the Ten Commandments; but this answer did not satisfy the one who asked, and he answered in turn that he had known these commandments from childhood.

10.13.0.en: "Then Jesus beholding him loved him": when Christ saw in this man the eagerness of his question, his humility in his worship, his real concern to keep the commandments from his youth, his attempt to apply them faithfully and sincerely, and his desire to inherit eternal life, He looked at him with a look of love and encouragement before presenting the cure to him and putting His finger on the real sickness of this rich man, which was love of money. Therefore the cure was the complete uprooting of the sin, that he give up his money to the poor, and it would become for him a treasure and a crown in the Kingdom of God. And despite the difficulty of the cure, the Lord Christ did not lighten any of it, but added to it that he follow Him, giving up indulgence and luxury, bearing the cross of self-denial and the acceptance of suffering ... Therefore the man was sad, for he felt the dominion of money over him; and instead of following Christ, he went away grieved!!

10.13.1.en: My God and my Lord ... I feel in my depths that I have not yet been freed from the love of money, indeed I am this very man ... for I fear and am troubled if anything is lost to me ... You are pointing to my sickness and not his, so will You give me healing?! I beg You, free me from this love that veils You from me, and satisfy me with You, so that all I possess becomes cheap under Your feet, and Your cross becomes the desire of my heart...

10.14.0.en: In follow-up and comment on the dialogue with the rich man, the Lord Christ spoke of the difficulty of the entrance of those who have riches into the Kingdom of God. And when He noticed the disciples' bewilderment and confusion, He made it clearer to them that money in itself is not a sin, but love of money, reliance on it, boasting in it and hoarding it makes a man depend on it more than on God, and even hardens his heart toward those around him, and the pride of wealth enters him, and he forgets his humility, his need and his thanksgiving to God. And to make clear the difficulty of the salvation of those who rely on their money, Christ gave them a pictorial example, that the passing of a camel - with all its size - through the eye of a needle is easier than the entrance of these into the Kingdom of Heaven, that is, the impossibility of the salvation of everyone who has put money in his hope...

10.14.1.en: My beloved brother ... do not forget that there were righteous rich men, such as Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus, and the Lord did not ask them to leave their money. The sin, then, that dwells in our depths in the midst of this material world, is the love of money itself, and it prevents us from seeing the work of God, so let us repent of it. And instead of wishing for wealth, let us wish for what is more lasting and useful, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys, and that is the Kingdom prepared for us by our rich Father.

10.15.0.en: When the disciples saw the difficulty of what Christ was teaching, they expressed what was inside them about the difficulty of salvation, saying one to another: "Who then can be saved?" Christ's answer came reassuring: what man cannot do in his striving, God completes by His grace. But we must be faithful in presenting our weaknesses to Him and our longing for the Kingdom, and He is able to complete His salvation in us, for with God all things are possible.

10.16.0.en: Spontaneously, and as usual, Peter was the quickest of those who spoke with Christ. And perhaps the awesomeness of Christ's last talk is what moved him to seek reassurance for himself and the disciples, who had left all to follow Christ.

10.16.1.en: "An hundredfold": Christ's answer came explaining and confirming the goodness of God, the maker of good things ... can God be indebted to a man?! For everyone who has left anything for the sake of God and service shall have a hundredfold, and the expression here is figurative, a way of saying the abundance of God's giving to whoever has left and followed Him, so He gives him here spiritual brothers and children, and peace of heart and a rest the world does not know, and He does not leave them in need of any of the necessities of the present material world either, although the matter is not free of persecution and afflictions in this time. But the lasting and permanent compensation is the inheritance of eternal life prepared by God Himself, and they will have a special and distinguished standing, and be nearer to God their Savior and more satisfied with Him...

10.16.2.en: My beloved brother ... is not this promise of Christ encouraging to us all to give up some of our comfort, our time and our money, in order to go on with Him in following and in true heartfelt spiritual service ... do you not long with me for the taste of the hundredfold?! Come then, come to the Church, and offer even a little of your time for service, for Christ needs all energies for His Church.

10.17.0.en: The Lord ended His words here with a warning, for the promise of the Kingdom to whoever has left does not create carelessness about the assurance of salvation, but we must be on guard, and complete our striving to the end. Was not Judas among those who left and followed Christ? Yet he turned back and fell away, and loved money and so betrayed Christ! For slackness and carelessness make the one who came later get ahead of the one who was first.

10.18.0.en: The disciples were like the rest of the Jews, for they understood all of Christ's talks about the Kingdom of Heaven and the Kingdom of God with a material, earthly and limited temporal picture, and the idea of positions and offices occupied some of them. Therefore this dialogue and the request of James and John to sit in the foremost place, that is, on the right and on the left of Christ.

10.18.1.en: "We desire": the verb came in the past tense to indicate either that the two disciples had already made the same request before, or a reference to the fact that their mother had already made the same request.

10.19.0.en: "Ye know not": Christ's answer came to make clear the difference between God's plan in the salvation of man, passing through the cross and its sufferings, and man's limited thinking, tied to earthly things and their passing glories. And the Lord completed His talk with a question to the two disciples, whose meaning is: are you able to bear My sufferings on the cross, and to drink the cup of injustice and humiliation to its end?!

10.20.0.en: "And they said unto Him, We can": without awareness, the answer came quickly and without understanding of Christ's purpose. Therefore Christ answered them with what they would understand later, namely that fellowship in suffering and death would indeed be granted to them, but sitting on His right hand and on His left is for the one who loves God, and strives with more labor and struggle; for God in His justice shows no partiality, and gives each one "according to his own labour" (1 Cor 3:8).

10.21.0.en: These human feelings, and not spiritual ones, were still master of the situation, for indignation filled the rest of the disciples. And when Christ noticed this, He began to correct their mistakes, explaining to them the concepts of true greatness in His kingdom, and that the greatness of the world is lordship, controlling others and exercising authority over them.

10.22.0.en: But what I ask of you is true humility. For whoever gives himself and his honor in the service of others becomes great before God. And whoever wants a high standing in the Kingdom must give up his pride, as though he were a slave with no rights. And remember this always, that you follow My example in My Incarnation, for I came giving up My glory, and I sought honor from no one, but served all in true self-giving unto death.

10.22.1.en: My beloved God ... what You truly did during Your Incarnation was beyond the imagination and understanding even of the angels, but this is Your infinite love and humility ... my God, make me ashamed of my self, which is still seeking its standing and its worldly glory ... make me always lift my eyes toward Your cross, so that it may be my example, that I may set out to serve those around me, giving myself as You did ... Amen.

10.23.0.en: Passing through Jericho on the way to Jerusalem, blind Bartimaeus heard of Christ's passing, and his cry "Jesus, Thou Son of David, have mercy on me" declared a faith that surpassed many ... for the title "Son of David" is the title of the Messiah the Savior, so he declared and believed in the One whom the priests and Pharisees had rejected. And his hope of healing at His hands is faith in the power of this Savior over all things.

10.24.0.en: When he cried out for mercy, many rebuked him...

10.24.1.en: Does not Satan do this with us, trying to silence us from repentance and from asking for mercy? Would that we did as he did and increased our crying out toward God, so that we may win His mercies and His healing for our souls.

10.25.0.en: "And Jesus stood still": and how could He not stand?! He who is overcome by His tenderness and His love for mankind, and He called the crying one in need. So the blind man cast away his garment - the garment symbolizes man's laziness - and came to Jesus, the fountain of our healing.

10.26.0.en: Despite the clarity and expectedness of the blind man's request, Christ asked him: "What wilt thou that I should do unto thee?"

10.26.1.en: And this reminds us of the sick man at Bethesda whom Christ asked: "Wilt thou be made whole?" (Jn 5:6). So Christ wants to teach us something important, namely that man must always declare his will and his insistence before God, whatever his weakness, and Christ is able to cure this weakness or helplessness ... Therefore this man received his healing because of his faith and his insistence ... and he followed Jesus in the way, that is, in His entry into Jerusalem.

10.26.2.en: Would that we learned, my brother, from this blind man how to cry out to God, and let nothing stop us until we obtain what we hope for from Him, especially the salvation of our souls.

10.26.3.en: Christ's entry into Jerusalem, the cursing of the fig tree, the cleansing of the temple
